summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results vs their current baseline provider. Redwood's Dedicated config shows consistent improvements in p95 latency (~180ms vs baseline ~320ms for 1k prompts) and higher sustained throughput (approx 4.5k tokens/sec vs 2.8k). We saw variance on long-context (16k) tail latency where caching + batching helped but tokenization differences caused some outliers. Quality tradeoffs after 4-bit quantization were minimal on our test prompts but NovusData will run their eval set. Security/compliance asks remain: SOC2 docs, SSO/SAML, audit log retention. Next steps include sharing raw logs, running extended tail tests, and lining up security reviewers.
topics: Batching and KV prefix caching effects
transcript:
[00:00] Alice Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick rollcall?
[00:06] Priya Nair: Priya here, CTO at NovusData. Samir and Liam are with me.
[00:10] Samir Patel: hey all, Samir.
[00:12] Liam O'Connell: Liam, eng manager.
[00:15] Marcus Li: Marcus from Redwood, SE. we've got the benchmark sheet up to date, i can walk through highlights.
[00:22] Alice Chen: perfect. so main agenda -- results vs baseline provider, any tuning notes, and next steps.
[00:30] Marcus Li: ok starting slide 1, we ran the baseline on CloudServe equivalently sized nodes (H100 equiv) and our Dedicated instances on A100-80GB pools configured with continuous batching and KV prefix caching. numbers are median across three runs.
[00:45] Marcus Li: for 1k prompt length: Redwood p50 ~60ms, p95 ~180ms, p99 ~320ms; baseline p95 was ~320ms and p99 ~560ms. throughput sustained tokens/sec: Redwood ~4500, baseline ~2800.
[01:05] Priya Nair: those p95 numbers look good; are these end-to-end including network overhead?
[01:10] Marcus Li: yes these are end-to-end including SDK call time, small NAT/egress cost simulated; we tried to match their test harness. small caveat - our tests used prefix cache warm for repeated prefixes; cold cache numbers are higher.
[01:24] Samir Patel: what about the 4k and 16k tests? our workload is often long context.
[01:30] Marcus Li: 4k was solid: Redwood p95 ~220ms; baseline ~450ms. 16k we saw larger variance: Redwood p95 ~1.2s but p99 spikes up to 3.6s on a couple outliers; baseline p99 was similar magnitude but average throughput was lower. the big win for us was throughput on sustained parallel requests.
[01:55] Liam O'Connell: those 16k spikes worry me - what caused the outliers?
[02:00] Marcus Li: a few causes: tokenization differences lead to longer effective sequence lengths on some inputs, and we observed a couple of runs where KV cache warm wasn't fully primed due to the harness timing. also, quantization variation - we used 4-bit q8_0 profile which is aggressive but faster.
[02:18] Alice Chen: to add, the orchestration layer will route some requests to slightly different kernels depending on seq len which creates small jitter - but it's deterministic once cached.
[02:30] Priya Nair: can you re-run with our eval set? the public prompts are not 1:1 with our production.
[02:35] Marcus Li: yeah, we asked for the eval set last week, didn't get it yet. if you drop it in the shared drive Marcus will re-run.
[02:42] Samir Patel: i uploaded a small slice earlier today, check the folder "novus-eval-v1" - maybe that wasn't in the sheet.
[02:48] Marcus Li: got it, i'll pick that up after this call.
[02:52] Marcus Li: another interesting point - when we enabled continuous batching with a 20ms window and token-based packing, throughput improved ~30% with only ~10-15ms extra p50 latency. so for NovusData's throughput-first endpoints it's a good trade.
[03:09] Alice Chen: cost discussion - roughly speaking, because of higher throughput Redwood's per-token cost in the POC runs is ~20% lower than the baseline when batching is used. raw, non-batched per-token cost is close to baseline.
[03:22] Liam O'Connell: can you share the cost calc? our finance wants TCO over 6 months.
[03:27] Alice Chen: yes i'll send the workbook, it's in the docs link in the sheet.
[03:32] Priya Nair: security, quick check: we need SOC2 type II, SSO/SAML, audit logs for 90 days, and KMS integration. any blockers?
[03:42] Marcus Li: we have SOC2 artifacts ready to share; SAML SSO supported via Okta. audit logs can be exported to your SIEM, retention configurable. KMS/HSM support is available on private deployment - for dedicated there are managed KMS options.
[03:56] Samir Patel: does the dedicated offering keep any customer data on disk?
[04:00] Marcus Li: no persistent model inputs are stored; logs and traces are available per retention policy and can be disabled or forwarded. we can provide an architecture doc.
[04:10] Priya Nair: perfect. one more on model quality - you mentioned quantization gave small regressions?
[04:16] Marcus Li: minimal on our fidelity tests for the target model. on some edge-case prompts we saw hallucination risk slightly higher after aggressive 4-bit q, likely due to subtle distributional shifts. recommended approach: run quantized profile on your eval set and compare with baseline for a set of NLG metrics.
[04:33] Samir Patel: we'll run that. also curious - competitor name was CloudServe in the sheet, right?
[04:38] Alice Chen: yes CloudServe is their current vendor. we kept vendor naming generic in public docs.
[04:43] Marcus Li: i want to call out an intermittent issue we saw in run #2 where kernel selection timed a microsecond anomalies that amplified under a specific token mix; patch is in CI and we can re-run with that build if you want.
[04:58] Liam O'Connell: please re-run with the patch, we want to see stable p99 behavior before committing.
[05:03] Marcus Li: will do.
[05:05] Alice Chen: timeline-wise, we propose: raw logs + sheet by Thu (Alice), targeted 16k tail runs by Sat (Marcus), security review kickoff mid next week. if all good, pilot expand early May.
[05:20] Priya Nair: sounds reasonable.
[05:22] Samir Patel: quick question about network egress - when you say end-to-end, we simulate internal traffic but our real host has private VPC peering, any difference?
[05:32] Marcus Li: negligible if peered; our external numbers include typical NAT overhead. with VPC peering we often see a 5-10ms improvement.
[05:40] Priya Nair: we also want longer retention on logs for at least 180 days for compliance - is that doable?
[05:46] Marcus Li: yes with an add-on for retention; we can include in the quote.
[05:50] Liam O'Connell: are there any known regressions vs baseline on model output quality?
[05:54] Marcus Li: not on our samples; the biggest delta is sometimes tokenization boundary handling which can change token counts and influence prompts. but that's rare and we can normalize tokenization in preproc.
[06:05] Alice Chen: ok let's open for Qs.
[06:08] Samir Patel: regarding the 16k outliers - do you have per-layer profiler traces? that would help us see where time is spent.
[06:14] Marcus Li: yes we can share profiler traces, they're in the raw logs zip. note that traces are sometimes noisy because of sampling.
[06:23] Priya Nair: if we see regressions on our eval, what's rollback plan?
[06:28] Alice Chen: we can pin to previous non-quantized model in the cluster, can do canary traffic split 10/90 for 24-48h then fully roll back if needed.
[06:36] Liam O'Connell: ok good.
[06:38] Marcus Li: action items recap: i'll run patched 16k tests and share the p99 histograms; Alice will share costs and raw logs; Priya to confirm security reviewers.
[06:50] Alice Chen: any other items?
[06:53] Priya Nair: no, thanks all.
[06:55] Alice Chen: great, we'll follow up in email, thanks.
[06:58] (call ends)

Notes: transcription has occasional speaker mis-attribution; some technical terms appear as "K V cache" or "q4_0" spelled inconsistently. Deck + benchmark sheet links: https://redwood.example.com/poc/novus/benchmarks and shared drive folder "novus-eval-v1".
